                <h1>Trump told us to be quiet. Never!</h1>
                <p>When <em class="italic-text">The Independent's</em> White House correspondent Andrew Feinberg asked a fair, necessary question in the Oval Office, he was called a "sick person," told to "be quiet," and hit with personal attacks from the very top of government.
We don't back down from powerful interests, and we don't stay silent when challenged. Real, uncompromised journalism requires independence and that depends on readers like you.</p>
                <p><strong class="bold-text">Don't let them silence the truth. Stand up for fearless reporting and support our independent journalism today.</strong></p>

  carries on looking exactly as the reader left it. When they have moved to a new
  section, useButtonNavScroll then animates from here to the new active item —
  which is why this must not centre that item itself. On the first page of a
  session there is nothing recorded, so the active item is centred directly.

  Centring is idempotent, so a page carrying two navs (and therefore two copies
  of this script) simply re-measures an already-positioned row for no effect.

  Deliberately measured rather than delegated to `scrollIntoView`, which also
  scrolls the element's vertical ancestors and would move the page itself.

  A hidden active item (the header's "More" below laptop) has nowhere to be
  centred, so the row rests at its start — as it does after a page that left it
  there, so the new active item animates in from the start (see TECH-5202).

      const scrollKey = list.getAttribute(listAttribute);

      const activeItem = list.querySelector('[' + activeItemAttribute + ']');
      const isActiveItemHidden =

      if (isActiveItemHidden || lastActiveItem === restAtStart) return;
